text.p: Morgan Stockbroking Ltd recommended Lihir Gold Ltd as a buy ahead of the Papua New Guinea miner's expected production start-up date,
"Buy for the gold resource and reserve base with production to commence in mid-1997," Morgan's head of research, Chris Brown said in a report.
Lihir was developing a resource containing 42.5 million ounces of gold with a mineable reserve of 25.2 million ounces at a cut-off grade of 1.5 grams per tonne, Brown said.
"On the basis of this resource, Lihir Gold is a world-ranked gold company," Brown said.
Placer Dome Inc and Homestake Mining Co were the only companies listed on the Australian Stock Exchange with a bigger resource base, Brown said.
"In terms of projected production in 1998, Lihir will rank amongst the largest Australian gold producers," he said.
Gold production from Lihir's oxide ore was expected from May 1997 to produce 120,000 ounces over 12 months.
Production of 550,000 ounces was projected in 1998 rising to 651,000 ounces in the second full year of production, he said.
Good exploration potential existed in the exploration acreage surrounding the special mining lease, Brown said.

Lihir's feasibility study had projected cash operating costs of US$213 an ounce through the mining period of 14.7 years and US$272 an ounce had been projected for the treatment of the stockpile over the balance of the 35-year project life, he said.
"These projected costs are based on the current production schedule," he said.
Optimisation of treatment process, higher-than-budgeted plant availability or increased metallurgical performance would result in lower costs.
"We expect that an increase in throughput resulting from an expansion of the plant would also result in lower cash costs."
Lihir had a strong balance sheet and was in a strong position to repay debt, Brown said.
He forecast a net profit in the year ended June 30, 1997 of A$20.6 million, rising to A$52.8 million in 1997/98 and A$107.9 milion in the year to June, 30, 1999.
"Investors should focus on the resource and reserve base," Brown said.
"The long production profile offers substantial upside from strengths in the gold price cycle," he said.
Based on prospectus forecasts, a cash flow multiple of 10 times would justify a market capitalisation for Lihir of US$3 billion, equivalent to a share price of above A$4 a share, Brown said.
Lihir shares last traded at A$2.20 at 0525 GMT (4.25 p.m.), up 2.0 cents from Tuesday's close.
